title: Microsoft backs Kerala edtech startup Wayvida with 3.25 crore support to accelerate AI innovation
description: Thiruvananthapuram (Kerala) [India], September 28 (ANI): Kerala-based EdTech startup Wayvida has received 3.25 crore in Microsoft cloud credits, supporting the company's plans to expand its AI-powered education technology platform. The support is expected to assist Wayvida in scaling its technology infrastructure and advancing its plans to take its AI-powered solutions to international markets. Founded by Gireesh

title: Microsoft Drops Copilot+ PC Branding While Retaining Key AI Features
description: Microsoft appears to be moving away from the Copilot+ PC branding for its Windows computers, two years after introducing the name to define a new category of AI-focused PCs. The company’s latest Surface devices no longer carry the Copilot+ PC label, although they continue to meet the hardware requirements and support the associated AI features. New Surface PCs Drop Copilot+ PC Label According to a report by Windows Central, Microsoft confirmed that its latest Surface computers are not being called Copilot+ PCs. Microsoft Surface Corporate Vice President Brett Ostrum said the new devices still meet the requirements that previously defined the category and continue to support Copilot+ features. Microsoft introduced Copilot+ PCs in 2024 alongside Qualcomm as a new category of Windows computers designed around AI capabilities. The devices were required to meet specific hardware standards, particularly for neural processing unit (NPU) performance, and initially offered AI features that were not available on other Windows PCs. Microsoft’s 2026 Surface PCs no longer include the Copilot+ PC name in their product titles, unlike earlier models. Compatibility references now largely appear in specification details instead. Hardware Requirements Remain The change appears to involve the branding rather than the underlying hardware requirements. Qualcomm Senior Vice President of Compute Kedar Kondap said the Copilot+ PC category was created around a hardware threshold for NPU-based experiences, including a 45 TOPS NPU. Manufacturers can continue offering those capabilities without using the Copilot+ PC name. Microsoft also shifted its messaging towards broader AI capabilities, including AI processing on the device and hybrid experiences that combine local and cloud-based computing. The latest Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch models continue to meet the requirements associated with the Copilot+ category. Their specifications therefore remain aligned with the hardware standards, even though Microsoft stopped using the label prominently. Also Read: Microsoft Drops the Copilot+ PC Label, Keeps the Tech Underneath Copilot+ Branding Sees Wider Pullback Microsoft’s move follows a broader decline in the use of the Copilot+ PC branding among PC makers. The report noted that Nvidia did not use the Copilot+ PC branding for its upcoming RTX Spark platform, despite RTX Spark systems meeting the category’s specification requirements. The Copilot+ PC category also faced challenges following its launch. Microsoft’s Recall feature, one of its key offerings, came under scrutiny from security researchers over concerns about how sensitive information was handled. Microsoft subsequently delayed its release. For now, Microsoft’s decision does not indicate that Copilot+ hardware requirements or features are being discontinued. Instead, the company appears to be placing less emphasis on the Copilot+ PC name while continuing to support the underlying AI capabilities.
